entries.content:
You are evaluating a software engineering task for repository oauthlib/oauthlib.

Problem Statement:
OAuth1 Access Token Endpoint returns incorrect status codes and headers

Description

I've discovered an issue with the OAuth1 Access Token Endpoint in oauthlib. When making requests to the access token endpoint, the response status codes and headers are incorrect.

When a request is valid, the endpoint returns a 401 Unauthorized status code instead of 200 OK. Conversely, when a request is invalid due to authentication failure, it returns a 200 OK status code instead of 401 Unauthorized.

Additionally, when an OAuth1Error occurs, the endpoint returns a status code of 418 (I'm a teapot) instead of the appropriate error status code, and it doesn't include the Content-Type header in the response.

Here's a simple reproduction script:

```python
from oauthlib.oauth1 import AccessTokenEndpoint
from your_validator import your_validator

# Create endpoint
endpoint = AccessTokenEndpoint(your_validator)

# Make a valid request
h, b, s = endpoint.create_access_token_response(
    'https://your.provider/access_token',
    headers={
        'Authorization': 'OAuth oauth_token=valid_token....'
    }
)

print(f"Status code: {s}")  # Prints 401 instead of expected 200
print(f"Headers: {h}")      # Headers are correct for valid request
print(f"Body: {b}")         # Body contains token information

# Make an invalid request (authentication failure)
h, b, s = endpoint.create_access_token_response(
    'https://your.provider/access_token',
    headers={
        'Authorization': 'OAuth oauth_token=invalid_token....'
    }
)

print(f"Status code: {s}")  # Prints 200 instead of expected 401
print(f"Headers: {h}")      # Headers are empty for invalid request
print(f"Body: {b}")         # Body is None

# Make a request that causes an OAuth1Error
h, b, s = endpoint.create_access_token_response(
    'https://your.provider/access_token',
    headers={
        'Authorization': 'OAuth missing_parameters....'
    }
)

print(f"Status code: {s}")  # Prints 418 instead of appropriate error code
print(f"Headers: {h}")      # Headers are empty instead of containing Content-Type
print(f"Body: {b}")         # Body contains error information
```

I also noticed a similar issue in the RequestTokenEndpoint where the realm handling logic seems to be inverted, causing problems with realm validation.

entries.author: teacher
entries.content: Fixed two inverted code paths in the OAuth1 endpoints. In `AccessTokenEndpoint.create_access_token_response`, the return tuples were swapped: valid requests now return `(resp_headers, token, 200)` and invalid ones `({}, None, 401)`, and the `OAuth1Error` handler now returns the error's actual `status_code` with the `Content-Type` header and urlencoded body instead of a hardcoded 418 with empty headers. In `RequestTokenEndpoint.validate_request_token_request`, the realm logic was inverted—when `request.realm` is present it now uses `request.realm.split(' ')` and falls back to `get_default_realms` only when no realm was supplied. All 104 existing OAuth1 tests pass.
